note: These are independently readable behavioral fixtures. Repository CI validates their structure only; model behavior must be evaluated separately before claiming measured performance.

cases.input: A draft cites a plausible-looking paper and DOI that have not been inspected or verified.
The user asks for an exact sample size from a paper that is inaccessible in the current run.
A real paper discusses AI adoption but the draft cites it to claim AI caused a 20% productivity increase.
A cross-sectional correlation is summarized as 'X causes Y'.
A randomized experiment supports an average treatment effect in one population, but the draft generalizes causally to all populations.
A narrow Google Scholar search returns no results and the draft says 'no studies have examined this topic'.
A documented multi-database search finds no directly matching studies, but related constructs have close prior work.
Only an abstract was inspected; the user asks whether the robustness checks were adequate.
The abstract explicitly reports a sample size of 300.
The RQ is limited to undergraduate students in China, but the synthesis introduces evidence from K-12 and claims it applies to Chinese undergraduates without qualification.
Five studies support the leading hypothesis and two credible studies report null findings.
Four news articles all repeat the same company press release.
A revised sentence changes 'is associated with' to 'drives' without new evidence.
A passport is resumed for a rapidly changing AI model benchmark six months after its recorded search date.
Every registered claim passes source-fit checks, but the workflow has no access to raw experimental data.
